nodes.description: Patient neutrophils show anomalous N-glycomes with a marked loss of fucosylation on multi-antennary glycans and fewer Lewis X units, while O-glycans are unaffected. In murine Jagn1-deficient neutrophils, adhesion-relevant receptors (E-selectin ligands, CXCR2) are under-sialylated. Glycosylation of the G-CSF receptor itself is affected.

evidence.reference_title: JAGN1 deficiency causes aberrant myeloid cell homeostasis and congenital neutropenia.
evidence.snippet: JAGN1-mutant neutrophils of patients P7 and P8 exhibited anomalous N-glycomic profiles, characterized by a marked reduction in fucosylation of all their multi-antennary glycans

nodes.description: Indicated for G-CSF-refractory neutropenia, severe infection or MDS/AML. In the multicentre cohort it gave stable haematopoietic recovery and ended infections in all six transplanted patients, though two needed a second graft after autologous reconstitution. It does not correct bone disease.

evidence.snippet: AlloHSCT resulted in stable hematopoietic recovery and a cure for infections in all patients without severe treatment-related toxicity.

nodes.description: JAGN1 is also needed in antibody-producing cells: Jagn1 deficiency alters their ER, lowers antibody production and changes IgG N-glycosylation, including fucosylation in patients with JAGN1 loss-of-function variants. A minority of patients have reduced immunoglobulin levels, although the large cohort did not find a clinical antibody-deficiency phenotype.

nodes.description: Homozygous (rarely compound heterozygous) germline JAGN1 variants, most of them missense, plus start-loss (c.3G>A, p.Met1), nonsense and frameshift alleles. Depending on the allele, patient cells carry reduced or undetectable JAGN1 protein, or a mutant and likely non-functional protein.

nodes.description: JAGN1-deficient granulocytes show raised BiP and die more readily: patient neutrophils undergo apoptosis more often under staurosporine and depolarize their mitochondria quickly, and myeloid cells expressing patient JAGN1 mutants succumb to a calcium- and calpain-dependent death programme (seen on overexpression of the mutants, not on JAGN1 knockdown). How much this contributes to the neutropenia, relative to impaired G-CSF receptor signalling, is unresolved; the zebrafish model argues it is not the primary mechanism.

nodes.description: JAGN1 resides in the ER and binds the COPI coat (COPA, COPB2, COPG2), which mediates retrograde Golgi-to-ER vesicle transport. Without it, the ER of myeloid cells is enlarged and selected secretory cargo is handled abnormally, which is the shared upstream defect for the glycosylation, granule and ER-stress consequences below.

In the only two patients reported to receive it, GM-CSF did not raise neutrophil counts and both proceeded to transplantation. Not an established therapy.

nodes.description: Mice lacking Jagn1 in the hematopoietic system have neutrophils with altered glycosylation, defective migration, impaired cytotoxic granule formation and poor killing of Candida albicans, but unlike patients are not neutropenic.

The neutrophils that are produced function poorly: Jagn1-deficient murine neutrophils migrate, adhere and kill Candida albicans badly, and bone marrow cells from JAGN1-mutant patients show defective fungicidal activity. This qualitative defect adds to the numerical neutropenia in producing infection.

nodes.description: Patient neutrophils carry less G-CSF receptor, of reduced molecular weight because of defective N-glycosylation, and JAGN1 knockdown blunts G-CSF-induced STAT3 phosphorylation. A zebrafish jagn1b model places G-CSF receptor signalling, rather than ER stress or apoptosis, as the primary driver of the neutropenia. The weakened receptor pathway is the likely basis of the poor and dose-hungry response to recombinant G-CSF.

nodes.description: Missense variant more often associated with syndromic facial features and bone disease.
Start-loss variant found homozygous in the founding Algerian Sephardic families; the most frequent variant in the 32-patient cohort and not associated with syndromic features there.
Recurrent missense variant, enriched in Romanian patients (possible founder effect) and associated with severe periodontitis and some neurodevelopmental delay.
Knockdown, CRISPR editing or misexpression of a patient-mutation-bearing jagn1b gives a selective neutropenia with raised UPR gene expression and apoptosis, and impaired G-CSF receptor signalling.
